text:
maria: FYI: after last runtime patch, we see ~9-12% p50 token-latency regression on int8/4bit combo for long-context chats. Dumped profiles, but suspect calibration artifacts + KV warmup.
liam: Do you have perf profiles? last change touched kernel selector heuristics.
maria: linked profile: /prof/1876543210/int8-bench.html. Main diff: increased kernel fallthrough, added mixed-precision FP8 path for attention.
noor: Quick thought: calibration dataset might be skewed with too many short prompts; per-tensor quant makes more bias. Are we doing per-channel for weights?
devon: We run per-channel for weights, per-tensor for activations for int8 because of kernel constraints. Heard per-channel stabilized attention in prior runs.
sam: Can we try excluding 'chatty' short prompts as outliers? Outlier handling we had was top-1% token clipping.
maria: I ran calib variants: 'prod-sim-10k' (longer chats) vs 'web-pages-100k' (short docs). Prod-sim kept quality but throughput worse; web-pages had better perf but hallucination spikes.
liam: We need a quick experiment. Proposal: 1) per-channel weights + per-tensor activations, 2) add MAD-based outlier removal, 3) re-run kernel selection with batch size sweep.
noor: Agree. Also watch KV cache warmup: profiler shows cold-request token generation does extra memcpy on first KV fill causing p99 spike.
devon: Repro snippet:
```
python bench.py --model rwd/7B --quant int8 --calib-set prod-sim-10k --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --measure kv_warmup
```
sam: I can run 1-2 overnight. Quick vote: per-channel vs per-tensor for weights? :+1: per-channel, :-1: per-tensor
maria: I lean per-channel for matmuls, but need to ensure caches aligned. Also consider kernel alignment expectations (16-byte granularity).
liam: If per-channel is heavier on calibration compute, use mixed strategy: per-channel for first N layers (attention), per-tensor rest. Might avoid outlier propagation.
noor: Good idea. Also augment calib set with adversarial long-tail tokens: code, email headers, timestamps — they blow quant stats.
devon: I'll run 4 combos: A) per-tensor baseline, B) per-channel all, C) per-channel attention-only, D) per-channel + MAD clipping. Capturing quality + token-accuracy on eval set.
maria: Add KV prefilling test: simulate warm start by sending a 128-token prefix before measuring steady-state latencies.
sam: Can we A/B on routing? fallback to fp16 if batch small and int8 path slower.
noor: Let's avoid silent fallbacks unless logged. Add flag: `quant_path=fallback_log_only`.
liam: Ok plan. Sam/Devon run experiments. Maria update release notes and rollback checklist. Regroup tomorrow 10am.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: experiment matrix created: /experiments/1876543210/matrix.csv :white_check_mark:
